speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to my office. I see you are experiencing intense itching and red bumps on your thigh and elsewhere; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms first started?

Have you noticed if the bumps appear in a specific pattern, such as lines or clusters, and do they tend to scratch when you aren't even touching them?

Do you have a known history of insect bites, recent travel to wooded areas, or contact with any unusual animals or plants?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential.
REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up clinical photograph of the rash on the thigh.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 37°C (98.6°F), Blood Pressure 130/85 mmHg, Heart Rate 72 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Skin Examination: Linear line with 3 red papules along the medial aspect of the right thigh; small rows of bumps on left leg and right forearm; excoriations present. Complete Blood Count: WBC 7,000 /μL (within normal limits), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL. Skin Scraping: No evidence of mites or eggs, ruling out scabies.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC is normal and the skin scraping ruled out scabies, but the linear arrangement of three red papules on your thigh is highly suspicious for a bed bug bite. Have you noticed any other small, dark specks (like dirt or tiny rust-colored dots) on your sheets or mattress seams? Additionally, do you have any known allergies or a history of eczema that might be worsening the itching?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bed Bug Bite Reaction (Cimicosis). The linear "breakfast, lunch, and dinner" pattern of red papules on your thigh, combined with your recent travel and the exclusion of scabies, strongly points to this diagnosis. While your medication history is noted, the specific morphology of the bites is the key differentiator here.
